open_points.subject: Function sandbox filesystem access
open_points.text: K-02 says a function has “no filesystem beyond its input”; A03 rule 1 gives it “one private exchange directory”, and rule 4 permits opening paths inside that directory.
open_points.question: May implementation code create, read, enumerate or modify files in the exchange directory, or is that directory accessible only to the runner?
options: Implementation code may use the bounded exchange directory as scratch space
Only the runner may access the exchange directory; implementation code receives inputs and outputs solely as Python objects
open_points.default_guess: Only the runner may access it, preserving K-02.

open_points.subject: Function access to clocks
open_points.text: K-02 says a function has “no clock”, while A03 rule 4 traps only a closed list that omits standard-library clock sources such as `time.clock_gettime`, `time.thread_time`, `os.times`, `resource.getrusage` and filesystem timestamps.
open_points.question: Are all ways of observing time forbidden, or only the entry points explicitly listed in A03?
options: Forbid every clock source and extend isolation/traps accordingly
Permit every clock source not present in the frozen trap list
open_points.default_guess: Forbid all clock sources because K-02 states the invariant.

open_points.subject: Deterministic function execution and admission
open_points.text: K-05 calls admission “a deterministic verdict”, and A03 requires “The same implementation on the same input yields the same output digest twice”, but permitted Python can observe nondeterministic facts such as object identities, scheduling and resource timing.
open_points.question: What exact determinism guarantee must the sandbox enforce, and how are permitted nondeterministic Python or OS observations handled?
options: Reject or isolate every observable nondeterministic source
Define determinism only as fixed evaluation rules over whatever execution outcomes occur
Remove the repeat-output guarantee
open_points.default_guess: Treat admission ordering and verdict calculation as deterministic, without promising byte-identical executions.

open_points.subject: Sandbox resource-bound semantics
open_points.text: A03 rule 5 says ResourceBounds are enforced with “`setrlimit` (address space, processes)” and that a “limit hit (memory, process count, scratch, `output_bytes`)” is `resource_exhausted`.
open_points.question: Are memory and process limits per process or aggregate across the whole sandbox, what counts toward scratch usage, and what observable event proves each limit was hit?
options: All bounds apply to the aggregate sandbox environment
`setrlimit` bounds apply per process while scratch/output are aggregate
Use implementation-specific enforcement semantics
open_points.default_guess: Apply every bound to the aggregate sandbox execution.

open_points.subject: Bubblewrap release dependency
open_points.text: A20 says “A release pins the exact versions of the kernel's Python dependencies and of the sandbox runtime”, while A03 requires only that `bubblewrap` “is present”.
open_points.question: Is the bubblewrap version also pinned or constrained, and what happens when the host supplies another version?
options: Pin an exact bubblewrap version
Declare a tested minimum/compatible range
Accept any version whose startup probe succeeds
open_points.default_guess: Require a release-pinned compatible version in addition to the probe.

open_points.subject: Existing admissions after a kernel runtime upgrade
open_points.text: A03 says the Python interpreter and standard library are “fixed by the kernel release”; A20 says a vulnerable dependency is answered by “a new release”; no rule says what happens to existing AdmissionVerdicts and Activations after that change.
open_points.question: After upgrading the Python runtime or sandbox dependencies, do existing admitted implementations remain active, require re-admission, or execute under their original runtime?
options: Keep existing activations and execute them under the new runtime
Invalidate verdicts and re-admit before execution
Retain each implementation's original runtime
open_points.default_guess: Require re-admission under the new runtime before an implementation can serve.

open_points.subject: Flow node identifier namespace
open_points.text: A05 rule 2 says “A flow input or flow output endpoint has the empty string as its node, so it orders before every node”, but no rule forbids an empty `node_id`.
open_points.question: May a flow node use the empty string, and if so how is it distinguished and ordered against flow endpoints?
options: Forbid an empty `node_id`
Use tagged endpoint kinds so an empty node id remains valid
Define a separate sentinel outside the string namespace
open_points.default_guess: Forbid an empty `node_id`.

open_points.subject: Cardinality versus value-schema validation
open_points.text: A13 says a `many` value is an array “each element of which must fit the port's `value_schema`”, while A09 says each response member “must validate against the port”; A03 and A04 likewise refer generally to a value fitting its port schema.
open_points.question: For a `many` value port, is `value_schema` applied to each element or to the array as a whole, especially when the schema itself has type `array`?
options: Validate each element against `value_schema`; cardinality supplies the outer array
Validate the whole array against `value_schema`
Require `value_schema` itself to describe the outer array
open_points.default_guess: Validate each element; cardinality supplies the outer array.

open_points.subject: Draft-write FlowActivation authority
open_points.text: M26 requires a draft-write attempt to name “the flow activation under which the run started”, but M19 and A12 pin only `flow_version_id` and function implementations, not the identity of the FlowActivation.
open_points.question: How is the exact FlowActivation recovered after the same version has been activated multiple times or after a restart?
options: Add the FlowActivation store position to the Run's pins
Infer the latest activation preceding the Run in store order
Use any activation of the pinned version
open_points.default_guess: Pin the exact FlowActivation position in the Run at creation.

open_points.subject: Approval request identity for multipart sends
open_points.text: State 0 says approval covers “the fully built request” and “Any difference at send” asks again; A10 rule 7 excludes the multipart boundary and the `content-length` value from the request description.
open_points.question: Does a changed multipart boundary or resulting Content-Length make a request different for approval purposes?
options: Yes; digest the exact wire request
No; multipart requests are identified by their semantic parts and derived length
Use a deterministic fixed boundary so no difference occurs
open_points.default_guess: Use a deterministic boundary and include the resulting Content-Length in the covered request.

open_points.subject: Retry after a direct `not_applied` outcome
open_points.text: K-08 and M26 say sending again after `not_applied` requires a fresh approval, but A09 maps a direct 4xx to `operation_refused`/`not_applied`, and A13 makes `operation_refused` a failure with no same-run retry action; A11 creates a new approval only when an `unknown` attempt is resolved `not_applied`.
open_points.question: Can a direct 4xx `not_applied` attempt be resent in the same run, and if so which action requests that resend? Is a later equal run considered a resend requiring fresh approval?
options: Direct 4xx permanently fails that run; a new run is independent
Direct 4xx waits for a fresh approval just like resolution to `not_applied`
Add an explicit retry action for failed `not_applied` attempts
open_points.default_guess: Direct 4xx fails the run; a separately started run is independent.

open_points.subject: Cancelling a running run
open_points.text: State 0 allows cancelling any run that is not finished, while A13 advances inside one request and A18 says “one request, including the run advancement it causes, ends before the next begins”.
open_points.question: Can the owner interrupt a run currently executing a function or HTTP request, or can cancellation apply only after the run has returned in a waiting state?
options: Cancellation is only possible for resting runs
Provide an out-of-band interrupt checked during advancement
Queue cancellation and apply it after the current node or request finishes
open_points.default_guess: Cancellation applies only to a run resting between requests.

open_points.subject: Credential secrecy against untrusted service responses
open_points.text: A17 says a credential “never enters the store, a record, a trace, a preview, a failure detail, a log line, a process argument or a response”; A09 allows an untrusted service's error body to be stored as `failure_detail` and successful bodies as output values.
open_points.question: What must the kernel do if a service echoes the credential value in an error or successful response?
options: Scan and refuse or redact any response containing the resolved credential
Limit the invariant to credentials inserted by the kernel, not equal bytes returned by a service
Trust services never to echo credentials
open_points.default_guess: Refuse to persist or return response content containing the resolved credential.

open_points.subject: Tokens and host paths inside user-controlled data
open_points.text: A16 rule 5 says agent text is “stored and returned verbatim”, while rule 7 says “No response carries a token, a service credential, a host path or a stack trace”.
open_points.question: Does rule 7 also prohibit returning user-supplied text or values that happen to contain a token or host-path string, and if so how are they detected and represented?
options: Rule 7 covers only kernel-originated authentication data, paths and diagnostics
Scan and redact matching tokens and path-like strings in all returned data
Refuse such input when authored
open_points.default_guess: Interpret rule 7 as applying only to kernel-originated sensitive material.

open_points.subject: Agent-token configuration hot reload
open_points.text: M27 says “a configuration repeating [an agent name] is refused at start”; A16 rule 2 says exactly three checks apply on re-read—parseability, token length and token uniqueness—and the changed token list then replaces the old one.
open_points.question: May a hot-reloaded token list contain duplicate or missing agent names, invalid `may_author` values, or a missing owner token, and how is the actor determined then?
options: Apply the full token-list schema and unique-agent-name checks on every re-read
Apply only the three listed checks and accept any otherwise parseable token-list shape
Require restart for changes other than token removal/addition within the existing shape
open_points.default_guess: Apply the complete token-list schema and unique-agent-name checks on every re-read.

open_points.subject: Service-credential reference resolution
open_points.text: M28 calls service credentials “references to secrets”; A17 says a reference “resolves to its value on the host” and later refers to “its secret file”, without defining the reference syntax or file-security rules.
open_points.question: What forms of credential reference are valid, how are they resolved, and what ownership, permission and symlink checks apply to the referenced secret file?
options: References are absolute file paths with the same ownership/no-symlink/private-mode checks as configuration
References use a named host secret provider
Any host path readable by the kernel is accepted
open_points.default_guess: Use explicit file references with owner-only permissions and no symlink traversal.

open_points.subject: Reading a manifest at `manifest_revision`
open_points.text: M28 provides `manifest_location` and `manifest_revision`; A08 says the record is read from a path “at the configured `manifest_revision`”, but defines no repository or snapshot access operation.
open_points.question: How does the kernel resolve a file at a revision, and what is refused when the location is not a repository, the revision is missing, or the working tree differs?
options: Read blobs directly from a specified Git revision
Require `manifest_location` to be an immutable directory already materialized at that revision
Treat the revision as metadata and read the current filesystem
open_points.default_guess: Read the exact file blob from the configured Git revision without using the working tree.

open_points.subject: Permitted `api_base_url` form and URL joining
open_points.text: A08 accepts any absolute `http` or `https` URL with a host; A09 constructs the target as “the `api_base_url` without a trailing `/` followed by the declared path”.
open_points.question: Are user information, query strings, fragments, percent-encoded separators and a base path allowed in `api_base_url`, and exactly how are they combined with the operation path?
options: Permit only scheme, host, optional port and an optional normalized base path; forbid userinfo, query and fragment
Allow every absolute URL and concatenate strings literally
Resolve the operation path using standard URL-reference rules
open_points.default_guess: Forbid userinfo, query and fragment; allow a validated base path and concatenate it literally with the declared path.

open_points.subject: Plain-HTTP loopback classification
open_points.text: A09 permits plain HTTP when the `api_base_url` “host is a loopback address”.
open_points.question: Does this mean only a literal loopback IP, or also names such as `localhost` or any hostname that resolves to loopback, and when is resolution checked?
options: Only literal IPv4/IPv6 loopback addresses
Literal loopback addresses and `localhost`
Any hostname whose current DNS result is exclusively loopback
open_points.default_guess: Allow only literal loopback IP addresses.

open_points.subject: Error-response failure detail encoding
open_points.text: A09 keeps up to `failure_detail_bytes_max` of an error response body as `failure_detail`; A20 says failure detail is cut “at a UTF-8 character boundary”, but error bodies are not required to be UTF-8.
open_points.question: How is an arbitrary binary or invalid-UTF-8 error body represented in `failure_detail`?
options: Decode as UTF-8 and replace invalid sequences
Store a bounded base64 encoding
Omit non-UTF-8 bodies
Store bytes rather than text
open_points.default_guess: Decode as UTF-8 with replacement and truncate the resulting text at a character boundary.

open_points.subject: EffectAttempt resolution time
open_points.text: M26 carries `recorded_at`, `concluded_at` and `resolved_by`, while A11 says changing `unknown` to `applied` or `not_applied` is “the only record of the resolution”; no `resolved_at` or update rule for `concluded_at` is given.
open_points.question: Which timestamp records the owner's resolution, and does `concluded_at` mean the original unknown outcome time or the later resolution time?
options: Add `resolved_at` and keep `concluded_at` as the transport outcome time
Overwrite `concluded_at` at resolution
Use no resolution timestamp
open_points.default_guess: Add `resolved_at` and preserve the original `concluded_at`.

open_points.subject: Capturing failures after refused or cancelled runs
open_points.text: State 0 says capture is refused when the execution succeeded, was skipped, belongs to another contract version, or “whose run was already released”; A15 permits capture only while the run still holds its spool, excluding every ended `refused`, `cancelled` or `succeeded` run even when the failed execution had only value inputs.
open_points.question: May a value-only failed function execution be captured after its run ended `refused` or `cancelled`, or is every such capture refused because the run no longer holds a spool?
options: Permit capture when all required inputs remain available, regardless of spool lifecycle
Permit capture only before the run ends or from an unreleased failed run
Keep value inputs but refuse only when a required file is gone
open_points.default_guess: Permit capture whenever all named inputs still exist; require a live spool only when file inputs are involved.

open_points.subject: Data-directory privacy check
open_points.text: A18 says the data directory “and everything in it are private to the kernel's user; the kernel refuses to start otherwise”.
open_points.question: Which owners and permission bits count as private for directories, database files, lock files, value files and spool files?
options: Require kernel-user ownership and no group/other permission bits
Require exact modes such as 0700 for directories and 0600 for files
Accept any access-control configuration that grants access only to the kernel user
open_points.default_guess: Require kernel-user ownership and no group/other permission bits, allowing stricter owner permissions.
